findings.note: Texans team preview (0 days old): Moreau scored two TDs in London last week, which gives him three on the season. It also says Sunday is WR Tank Dell's first game in 673 days, and Dell could take away some of the limited short targets. No injury news about Moreau was found.

Official game log, Weeks 1-5: 2, 2, 2, 1 and 2 catches (9 for 65 yards in 5 games, 3 starts). He went over 1.5 in four of five games, and the London two-TD game was presumably a fifth, but each over cleared by just one catch.

Covers game log: he got 2, 2, 4 and 1 targets in Weeks 1-4, about 2.3 a game, so the over usually needs him to catch nearly every look. The low volume fits a backup role, since ESPN called him depth behind starter Dalton Schultz when he signed.

RotoWire (Oct 5) says Metchie's five targets in Week 4 came while Jalen Coker was out with a quad injury and that he would go back to a rotational role once Coker was cleared. This week's status for Coker and Legette was not confirmed.

His game log shows 2, 3 and 2 catches in his last three games (Weeks 3, 4 and 6), 0 catches in Week 2, and inactive in Week 1. It also notes he has never had more than 29 catches in a season and was listed as the No. 5 WR and return man in September.

ESPN shows him active for Sunday's home game against Tampa Bay with 7 catches on 13 targets this season. In Week 6 at Philadelphia he had only 3 targets (2 catches), and ESPN's season projection is about 24 catches.

Dowdle is questionable for the Paris game with a new knee injury, separate from the toe issue that kept him out earlier. He was limited all week, and his status was expected with inactives 90 minutes before the 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff.

Dowdle was clearly the RB2 in his Week 6 return: Warren played 74% of snaps and had 14 carries to Dowdle's 7, though both got four targets. Covers picks Dowdle for an anytime TD (not receptions) and cites 16 mph winds in Paris.

ESPN's game log shows 3 catches for 9 yards in the Week 6 return at TB, and 7 catches across three games this season. Its fantasy note says he seems more likely than not to play, but expects him to share work with Warren.

Says Minnesota runs the ball at one of the NFL's highest rates, RB Jordan Mason is back at practice, and the Colts allow 4.7 yards per carry; both writers pick a lopsided Vikings win (26-10, 27-13), which suggests fewer late passes.
CBS Sports picks Vikings -6.5 and projects a 33-19 Minnesota win. If the Vikings lead comfortably, they will likely run more, which works against a high passing-attempt total for Murray.

ESPN's Solak says Murray will have Jefferson, Addison and Hockenson all healthy, and predicts Minnesota leads the league in scoring. Bowen notes Murray has 16 rushing attempts over his last two games, and those scrambles and runs can take away from his pass attempts.
